itineraries.title: Old Dhaka in a Weekend
itineraries.subtitle: Mughal forts, the Pink Palace & Louis Kahn
itineraries.seasonNote: Doable any season; coolest, clearest and least humid Nov–Feb.
itineraries.summary: Two days through the layers of the capital: the lanes of Old Dhaka with its unfinished Mughal fort, the Nawabs' riverside Pink Palace and the ghats of the Buriganga on day one, then the modern republic's two great monuments — Louis Kahn's National Parliament and the martyrs' memorial at Savar.

stops.name: Lalbagh Fort
stops.note: start early at the unfinished 1678 Mughal fort and the tomb of Pari Bibi

stops.name: Ahsan Manzil (Pink Palace)
stops.note: the domed riverside palace of the Dhaka Nawabs, now a museum

stops.name: Sadarghat & the Buriganga
stops.note: end the day among the launches and ferries at the city's old river port

stops.name: Dhakeshwari Temple
stops.note: the national temple and namesake of the city, a short hop from Lalbagh

stops.name: Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban (National Parliament)
stops.note: Louis Kahn's monumental concrete parliament, best seen from across its lake

stops.name: Jatiyo Smriti Soudho (National Martyrs' Memorial)
stops.note: the soaring Liberation War memorial at Savar, a half-hour drive northwest

itineraries.title: Mughal Capital & Sonargaon
itineraries.subtitle: From Lalbagh to the lost city of Panam
itineraries.seasonNote: Cool, dry weather for walking the open ruins and forts.
itineraries.summary: Three days tracing the old seats of power around the capital — the Mughal core of Dhaka, the abandoned merchant city of Panam at Sonargaon, and the riverside forts and ancient mounds of Munshiganj across the Dhaleshwari.

stops.name: Lalbagh Fort
stops.note: the unfinished 17th-century fort complex — budget a couple of hours

stops.name: Ahsan Manzil (Pink Palace)
stops.note: the Nawabs' palace on the Buriganga to close the day

stops.name: Panam Nagar (Panam City)
stops.note: walk the single street of crumbling merchant mansions at old Sonargaon

stops.name: Sonargaon Folk Art & Craft Museum (Boro Sardar Bari)
stops.note: the restored Sardar Bari mansion and the national folk-art collection

stops.name: Goaldi Mosque
stops.note: a single-domed pre-Mughal mosque hidden among the village fields

stops.name: Idrakpur Fort
stops.note: a compact Mughal river fort of 1660 in the heart of Munshiganj town

stops.name: Baba Adam's Mosque
stops.note: a six-domed mosque of 1483, one of the oldest in the region

stops.name: Nateshwar Buddhist Archaeological Site
stops.note: the excavated remains of an ancient Buddhist monastery and stupa

itineraries.title: Forests, Palaces & Terracotta
itineraries.subtitle: A north & west loop through Gazipur, Tangail & Manikganj
itineraries.seasonNote: Dry-season touring; the sal forests are greenest just after the monsoon.
itineraries.summary: Three days looping out from the capital through the sal forests and palaces of Gazipur, the terracotta mosques and zamindar estates of Tangail, and the grand Baliati mansion of Manikganj before the ferry back along the Padma.

stops.name: Bhawal National Park
stops.note: walk the trails of the sal forest just north of the city

stops.name: Bhawal Rajbari (Joydebpur)
stops.note: the sprawling estate at the heart of Bengal's famous 'lost prince' case

stops.name: Nuhash Polli (Pirozali)
stops.note: novelist Humayun Ahmed's wooded retreat, now open to visitors

stops.name: Atia Mosque
stops.note: a richly terracotta-decorated mosque of 1609, once on the 10-taka note

stops.name: Karatia Zamindar Bari & Saadat College
stops.note: the grand estate and college of the Karatia zamindars

stops.name: Mawlana Bhashani's Mazar & Santosh
stops.note: the tomb of the 'Red Maulana' beside the university he founded at Santosh

stops.name: Baliati Zamindar Bari (Baliati Palace)
stops.note: one of Bengal's most imposing zamindar complexes, a wall of columned facades

stops.name: Paturia Ferry Ghat
stops.note: watch the river traffic on the Padma before the return to Dhaka

itineraries.title: Padma Delta & the Father of the Nation
itineraries.subtitle: The great bridge, Tungipara & the river districts
itineraries.seasonNote: Dry season; rivers are calmer and ferry crossings smoother.
itineraries.summary: Five days across the south-western delta of the Dhaka division — beginning with the great Padma Bridge crossing into Shariatpur, then the shrines and lakes of Madaripur, the mausoleum of Bangabandhu at Tungipara, the poet's country of Faridpur, and the old Padma ferry town of Rajbari.

stops.name: Padma Bridge (Jajira Point)
stops.note: cross the landmark 6.15 km bridge and stop at the Jajira viewpoint

stops.name: Sureshwar Darbar Sharif
stops.note: a major riverside Sufi shrine and pilgrimage centre

stops.name: Dargah of Hazrat Shah Madar
stops.note: the medieval shrine that gives the district its name

stops.name: Shakuni Lake (Shukuni Dighi)
stops.note: the town's great heritage tank, ringed by a walking promenade

stops.name: Mausoleum of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman (Tungipara)
stops.note: the resting place and memorial complex of the founding leader

stops.name: Orakandi Thakurbari
stops.note: the Matua faith's holiest site, busy at the spring Baruni Snan festival

stops.name: House of Pallikabi Jasimuddin
stops.note: the riverside home and grave of the beloved 'folk poet' Jasimuddin

stops.name: Mathurapur Deul
stops.note: a tall, tapering brick tower of uncertain origin in the fields

stops.name: Daulatdia Ferry Ghat
stops.note: the vast Padma ferry terminal, gateway back across to Manikganj

stops.name: Godar Bazar (Padma Riverbank)
stops.note: the town's favourite riverside spot for an evening by the Padma

itineraries.title: The Eastern Edge — Ancient Ruins & the Haor
itineraries.subtitle: A 2,500-year-old city and the road across the wetlands
itineraries.bestSeason: Monsoon (June–September) for the flooded haor; Oct–Feb for dry-road touring
itineraries.seasonNote: The haor is at its spectacular best under monsoon water; the all-weather road is drivable year-round.
itineraries.summary: Two days along the division's eastern rim — the excavated 2,500-year-old fort-city of Wari-Bateshwar and the great cloth market of Narsingdi, then the mosques of Kishoreganj and the celebrated submersible road threading the Itna–Mithamoin–Austagram haor.

stops.name: Wari-Bateshwar Ruins
stops.note: the excavated remains of a fortified city dated to roughly 450 BCE

stops.name: Baburhat (Shekherchar) Cloth Market
stops.note: one of the largest wholesale cloth markets in the country

stops.name: Pagla Mosque
stops.note: the famous mosque whose donation boxes yield record sums when opened

stops.name: The Haor & Itna–Mithamoin–Austagram Road
stops.note: drive the submersible road across the open haor — magic at sunset

itineraries.title: Shariatpur Heritage Loop
itineraries.subtitle: Padma bridge, jinn mosque & zamindar ruins
itineraries.seasonNote: Best in the cool, dry months (Oct–Mar) for river weather and clear light; the Sureshwar Urs falls in early February.
itineraries.summary: Two days threading the old river country on the south bank of the Padma — from the great bridge at Jajira through Sadar's temples, the poet's house and Buri'r Hat mosque, then south to the legendary Jinn Mosque and east through Bhedarganj's ancient tank to Naria's crumbling zamindar manor and the Sufi shrine at Sureshwar. A loop traced straight from the district's own heritage map, broken by a plate of Haru Ghosh's famous roshogolla in Palong Bazar.

days.title: Sadar & the bridge — temples, poet's house & roshogolla

stops.name: Padma Bridge (Jajira Point)
stops.note: start at the Jajira approach near Naodoba for a clean view of the 6.15 km span

stops.name: Rudrakar Math
stops.note: the district's finest pre-modern temple — a ~150-year-old monastery spire

stops.name: Dhanuka Manasa Bari
stops.note: a ~600-year-old complex of Sultanate- and Mughal-era temples wrapped in serpent-goddess legend

stops.name: Kobi Rathindrakanta Ghatak Chowdhury's House
stops.note: the poet's two-storey family home with its old library, near Premtola — then break for Haru Ghosh's famous roshogolla at Palong Bazar

stops.name: Buri'r Hat Jame Masjid
stops.note: a 1907 mosque built with English cement and Kolkata stone, capped by a tall later minaret

days.title: South & the river — jinn mosque, ancient tank & the Sufi shrine

stops.name: Jinn Mosque (Talukdar Bari Jame Masjid)
stops.note: the ~400-year-old single-domed mosque at Shibpur that lore says jinns raised overnight

stops.name: Mahisarer Digambari Dighi
stops.note: a vast ~600-year-old tank beside a Digambari sannyasi's house in Bhedarganj

stops.name: Kartikpur Zamindar Bari
stops.note: an ornate, crumbling two-storey manor beside a stone-lined pond in Naria

stops.name: Sureshwar Darbar Sharif
stops.note: end at the great riverside Sufi shrine and pilgrimage centre on the Padma
